MLP/Others includes linear projections, spatial merging and pixel shuffle; Q-Former covers query-transformer connectors; Cross-Attention refers to bridges attending to separate visual features. Hybrid Adaptor covers combinations such as learned pooling plus projection, or projection plus visual experts inside the language backbone.

In this section: 4.1 Taxonomy by Generation Paradigm · 4.2 Any-to-Any / Omni UMMs · 4.3 Related Generators (U+G Unverified)
Models that unify multimodal understanding and visual generation within one framework. The defining property is U+G unification, not necessarily training from scratch.

This taxonomy first identifies how visual content is sampled, then records whether the described system also provides an autoregressive understanding/text-output path:
For example, Qwen-Image uses its Qwen-VL component as a condition encoder for MMDiT image sampling and is placed in Diffusion-Based. Qwen-Image-2.0 uses the same generation paradigm, but its U+G membership is unverified; it is retained separately as a related generator (§4.3). UniWorld (Fig. 3 and Table 1) explicitly retains an AR VLM understanding branch, evaluates image-to-text understanding, and pairs it with a flow-matching image generator, so it is placed in Hybrid. Merely inheriting a pretrained VLM does not prove that the resulting system exposes its standalone outputs.
Pixel, semantic, learnable-query, and hybrid encoding describe a separate representation dimension. Subsections retain these distinctions within a generation paradigm; entries using diffusion reconstruction decoders state that component explicitly.
